metadata.name: netstat
metadata.displayName: netstat - Print network connections, routing tables, interface statistics
metadata.description: Print network connections, routing tables, interface statistics

installation.note: netstat is part of the net-tools package, which is deprecated in favor of 'ss' and 'ip' commands, but still widely used

overview.summary: The netstat command displays network connections, routing tables, and network interface statistics. It's a legacy tool that's been largely replaced by 'ss' and 'ip' commands, but remains popular due to its widespread familiarity and comprehensive output. Useful for monitoring network activity, checking listening ports, and diagnosing network issues.

syntax.description: netstat can display different types of network information depending on the options used. Common uses include listing connections, showing listening ports, or displaying routing tables.

options.use_case: See all network connections including listening and established
See which ports are open and listening for connections

options.description: Show numerical addresses instead of resolving hosts
Show PID and name of program owning socket
options.use_case: Identify which process is using a port (requires root)
Monitor network interface activity and errors

misconceptions.title: Deprecated status
misconceptions.misconception: netstat is the modern way to check network connections
misconceptions.reality: netstat is deprecated. Modern alternatives are 'ss' (for sockets) and 'ip' (for routing). However, netstat is still widely available and used.
misconceptions.tip: Learn 'ss' and 'ip' commands for future-proof network administration

misconceptions.title: Requires root
misconceptions.reality: Basic netstat commands work without root, but '-p' (process info) requires root privileges
misconceptions.tip: Use 'sudo' when you need to see which process owns a connection

common_pitfalls.description: netstat may be slow due to DNS lookups
common_pitfalls.solution: Use '-n' option to show numerical addresses and skip DNS resolution

common_pitfalls.description: Process names not shown without proper permissions
common_pitfalls.solution: Use 'sudo' with '-p' option to see process information

common_pitfalls.description: Output can be overwhelming with many connections
common_pitfalls.solution: Use filters like '-l' for listening only, or pipe to 'grep' to filter results

related_commands.description: ss is the modern replacement for netstat, faster and more feature-rich
ip route show replaces 'netstat -r' for routing table
lsof -i can also show network connections and processes
iftop shows real-time network bandwidth usage

best_practices: Use 'ss' instead of netstat for better performance (modern replacement)
Combine '-tuln' for comprehensive listening port information
Use '-n' to avoid slow DNS lookups
Use '-p' with sudo to identify processes using ports
Pipe output to 'grep' to filter specific ports or addresses
Use '-c' for continuous monitoring of network activity
performance_tips: 'ss' command is significantly faster than netstat
Use '-n' flag to skip DNS resolution for faster output
For scripts, prefer 'ss' over netstat for better performance

additional_notes.deprecation: netstat is deprecated in favor of 'ss' and 'ip' commands, but remains widely used
additional_notes.installation: On newer Ubuntu systems, net-tools may not be installed by default. Use 'ss' as an alternative.
